prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: World University Rankings 2024: Top Seven (language en).
Grid: 7 columns × 9 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "University" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Country" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Score" spans 4 col × 1 row; "Overall rank" spans 1 col × 2 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "University" · longest unbreakable word 109px · one-line width 277px
  col 2: header "Country" · longest unbreakable word 61px · one-line width 111px
  col 3: header "Score › Teaching" · longest unbreakable word 65px · one-line width 65px
  col 4: header "Score › Research" · longest unbreakable word 67px · one-line width 67px
  col 5: header "Score › Citations" · longest unbreakable word 65px · one-line width 65px
  col 6: header "Score › Industry" · longest unbreakable word 60px · one-line width 60px
  col 7: header "Overall rank" · longest unbreakable word 51px · one-line width 86px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Rendering convention: the screenshot always shows the WHOLE table. Anything beyond the dashed box is not clipped; it is the part a reader reaches by scrolling sideways, so judge both what fits in the box at first sight and the cost of scrolling to the rest.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Compare the top seven universities by overall rank and four component scores, with country as context.","reading":"Readers identify a university, follow its row across to compare scores and rank, and scan down individual score columns to compare institutions. On a phone, horizontal scrolling separates some of those comparisons from the university names.","groups":["University and Country identify each institution and provide context.","Teaching, Research, Citations and Industry are parallel measures under the shared Score header and should have comparable widths.","Overall rank summarizes position and should remain easy to distinguish from the component scores."],"keep_intact":["University names as recognizable word sequences, without splitting individual words where possible.","Country names and individual numeric scores.","Rank numbers and the individual words in column headers."],"may_wrap":["University names can wrap at spaces; longer names can use multiple lines.","United Kingdom and United States can wrap between words.","Overall rank can wrap between its two words.","The two-tier score header already creates height that can accommodate wrapping in University, Country and Overall rank."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r2A: widths [130, 82, 86, 88, 86, 81, 72] · table 626×537px · row heights [36, 36, 60, 60, 83, 60, 60, 60, 83] · column headers wrapped 1/8 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 266px
Design r2B: widths [180, 82, 86, 88, 86, 81, 72] · table 676×513px · row heights [36, 36, 60, 60, 83, 60, 60, 60, 60] · column headers wrapped 1/8 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 316px

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}

log.raw: {"critique":[{"design":"r2A","good":"The compact university column keeps every word intact while leaving Teaching fully visible and most of Research visible at first sight. This may improve name wrapping at a smaller cost to the initially visible Research column."},{"name":"single-line-country","widths":[130,132,86,88,86,81,72],"change":"Test the alternative of keeping country names on one line while retaining the compact university column.
